name: Accelerator thermal interface
title: Keep thermal margin after cycling.
summary: Find whether the fix belongs in the interface material, mounting, coldplate or local coolant path.
owner: Server thermal team or cooling-module developer
problem: An assembly passes initially but develops a hotspot or thermal drift under representative loads and repeated heating. A real owner case is still needed.
value: Avoid changing the wrong part of an expensive accelerator assembly. The potential value is a qualified design change and fewer unnecessary prototypes; the saving is unmeasured.
change: Interface material, application, mounting load, plate or local fluid path.
measure: Temperature maps, heat input, surface form, mounting load, flow and pressure drop.
deliver: A repeatable assembly recipe that meets thermal, mechanical and hydraulic requirements after cycling.
evidenceSummary: OCP documents qualification methods. Purdue reports geometry-dependent grease degradation in a controlled surrogate. The combined diagnostic bench is our proposal.
scope: General qualification methods and a research surrogate; no current GB300 defect or exact factory route is established.

steps.title: Establish baseline
steps.subtitle: Geometry + repeatability
steps.action: Identify the accessible interface, inspect surfaces and assemble a traceable reference specimen. Calibrate the thermal and hydraulic rig.
steps.change: Repeat controlled mounts on separate specimens; keep an undisturbed control.
steps.measure: Surface form, force/displacement, applied power, temperatures, flow and fixture pressure loss.
steps.decision: Is the effect larger than measurement and assembly variation? Torque alone does not establish contact pressure.
steps.basis: Reference method; proposed combined baseline

steps.title: Reproduce drift
steps.subtitle: Load + power cycles
steps.action: Apply defined spatial heat patterns and owner-specified power cycles at controlled inlet conditions.
steps.change: Heat distribution and exposure; hold the assembly and coolant conditions controlled.
steps.measure: Local temperature rise and drift, inlet/outlet temperature, flow and differential pressure.
steps.decision: Which conditions reproduce the loss of margin? Record the aged assembly before remounting destroys evidence.
steps.basis: Mechanism and test infrastructure documented; campaign proposed

steps.title: Separate causes
steps.subtitle: Contact or coolant?
steps.action: Compare contact/material interventions against fluid-path interventions with known-good controls.
steps.change: One approved interface or hydraulic factor per discriminating experiment.
steps.measure: Thermal-map changes alongside pressure/flow and assembly records.
steps.decision: Does the evidence support mounting, material aging, fluid restriction or a combination? A lower temperature alone does not prove the cause.
steps.basis: Proposed interpretation and experiment selection

steps.title: Build a revision
steps.subtitle: Make the physical change
steps.action: Install the justified material, retention or plate variant and record its actual assembled condition.
steps.change: Material/application, retention hardware or approved geometry. New plates require fabrication.
steps.measure: Incoming geometry, material identity, assembly loads and initial thermal/hydraulic response.
steps.decision: Did the intended physical change occur, and did it produce the predicted effect?
steps.basis: Existing development methods; proposed orchestration

steps.title: Verify durability
steps.subtitle: Fresh builds + held-out loads
steps.action: Freeze the revision and repeat on independent builds, withheld conditions and the actual product.
steps.change: Fresh specimens and validation conditions; keep the requirements fixed.
steps.measure: Aged thermal margin, leak integrity, mechanical limits and repeatability.
steps.decision: Release only a reproducible, product-relevant solution. A passing representative heater cannot release the product.
steps.basis: Proposed verification campaign grounded in qualification methods

bench.specimen: One package-to-coldplate interface, its retention assembly and a defined local coolant branch.
bench.stimulus: Programmable representative heat source, controlled coolant supply and owner-defined cycling.
bench.hard: Dedicated thermal/fluid controls, deterministic protection, controlled dispensing and instrumented fastening establish repeatability.
bench.robot: Exchange identifiable specimens and plate variants; transfer to inspection; operate controlled fastening tools after fixtures are proven.
bench.flexible: Potential hose/cable presentation or variable connector handling. Useful only if a demonstrated task cannot be handled well by a fixture.
bench.llmDecision: Maintain competing explanations, propose a test that separates them, interpret the combined results and prepare the change record.
bench.tools: Numerical fitting, physics simulation and experiment optimization calculate results. Validated controllers operate equipment and enforce limits.
bench.wait: Thermal stabilization, drain/fill, new plate fabrication and reliability exposure remain physical waits.

verification: Preserve aged evidence before disturbing the interface.
Confirm the change on fresh assemblies and held-out conditions.
Demonstrate transfer from test vehicle to actual product.
baseline: Expert thermal engineering with the same integrated rig, CFD/FEA and conventional experiment planning. Existing cooling suppliers already combine design, prototypes and qualification.
access: An owner-controlled failing assembly, mechanical limits, material permissions and authority to change the interface and local cooling.
unknowns: Recurring owner failures and avoidable engineering effort
Sensor and test-vehicle fidelity on the actual package
Incremental value of the LLM beyond the same rig plus an expert
nextTest: Use one real initial-pass / aged-fail case to compare the current workflow, an integrated conventional bench, and that same bench with LLM-assisted experiment selection.

name: Power-converter transients
title: Recover transient margin without adding bulk.
summary: Resolve the control, capacitance and load-response tradeoff inside a high-density AC/DC converter.
owner: Converter design team with firmware and circuit authority
problem: Repeated load steps push the internal bus towards protection limits or cause unacceptable output deviation. More capacitance may conflict with density targets.
value: Find a stable design or control change across the operating envelope, avoiding repeated hardware revisions. No unresolved customer case or commercial saving is established.
change: Approved control/feed-forward parameters and capacitor-bank or connection variants.
measure: Synchronized internal bus voltage, output voltage/current, input waveforms and protection events.
deliver: A reproducible hardware/firmware revision meeting transient, thermal and input-quality limits.
evidenceSummary: Infineon describes reduced-capacitance load-step constraints and a successful feed-forward implementation. Our proposed bench would address a new owner-specific case.
scope: An AC/DC reference design, not a confirmed Lenovo PSU route or an 800 V DC/DC design.

steps.title: Capture the failure
steps.subtitle: Validate load fidelity
steps.action: Reproduce an owner-supplied failing load transition on an instrumented converter.
steps.change: Defined load amplitude, slope and repetition within the allowed envelope.
steps.measure: Actual load current, bus/output voltage and protection flags with synchronized instruments.
steps.decision: Does the physical stimulus reproduce the failure, and can the acquisition resolve the fast event?
steps.basis: Reference transient tests; owner campaign proposed

steps.title: Separate mechanisms
steps.subtitle: Control, energy or path?
steps.action: Compare relevant internal waveforms with the schematic, firmware and thermal state.
steps.change: Load timing relative to AC phase, source conditions and approved temperature conditions.
steps.measure: Input current/voltage, branch currents where accessible, Vbulk, Vout and controller events.
steps.decision: Does the fault point to control latency, energy storage, sensing or connection impedance?
steps.basis: Proposed multi-signal diagnosis

steps.title: Change the design
steps.subtitle: Firmware + hardware
steps.action: Apply a bounded control revision or install an approved component variant after verified isolation and discharge.
steps.change: Feed-forward/filter settings or a keyed capacitor/interface variant; preserve protection requirements.
steps.measure: Revision identity, connection checks and predicted waveform response.
steps.decision: Did the change address the proposed mechanism without introducing a new failure?
steps.basis: Reference control fix; broader bench proposed

steps.title: Sweep the corners
steps.subtitle: Source + load + temperature
steps.action: Repeat the test over a preregistered operating envelope and compare against the original design.
steps.change: Permitted source/load conditions and thermal state, not the acceptance criteria.
steps.measure: Transient limits, component temperatures, efficiency and input-current quality.
steps.decision: Is the benefit robust or merely tuned to one trace?
steps.basis: Proposed verification using documented electrical measurements

steps.title: Confirm the revision
steps.subtitle: Independent retest
steps.action: Restore normal chassis/cooling geometry and test held-out traces and independent builds.
steps.change: Representative installation and fresh verification units.
steps.measure: Owner performance limits plus the applicable release checks.
steps.decision: Accept a verified change. Formal EMC and safety qualification remain separate release gates.
steps.basis: Proposed release campaign; source EMI work is preliminary

bench.specimen: One editable AC/DC converter with approved internal test access.
bench.stimulus: Programmable AC source, high-bandwidth electronic load and deterministic switching.
instruments: Synchronized oscilloscope and appropriately isolated probes
bench.hard: Source/load sequencing, discharge verification, interlocks and fast protection. The converter controller retains real-time control.
bench.robot: Potential loading of standardized cartridges or fixtures after verified isolation. Qualified manual rework remains appropriate initially.
bench.flexible: No necessary role established. Variable harness or probe tasks would need their own reliability case.
bench.llmDecision: Reconcile electrical evidence with design context, choose a discriminating diagnostic branch and produce a traceable change-and-retest record.
bench.tools: Control models, circuit simulation and constrained numerical optimization do the quantitative work; validated hardware controls enforce the action envelope.
bench.wait: Discharge, rework, thermal equilibrium, fabrication and formal qualification remain. Fast waveform capture is not the full iteration time.

verification: Keep protection and performance requirements fixed.
Retest unseen traces and the restored product installation.
baseline: Converter engineers using scripted automated test, scopes, simulation and conventional experiment optimization. Successful feed-forward control already exists.
access: Internal test points, editable firmware/schematics, failing traces and authority to change the design. A sealed purchased PSU is insufficient.
unknowns: Benefit over current engineering and scripted test
nextTest: Replay a real failing case with synchronized measurements, then compare diagnosis and verified fixes using the same bench with and without LLM assistance.

name: Optical package reliability
title: Keep optical performance after bonding and stress.
summary: Find the material, attachment and package recipe that preserves optical-loss margin through the real assembly lifecycle.
problem: Good initial alignment does not guarantee good performance after bonding, reflow or environmental stress. A real candidate must expose that failure history.
value: Avoid a package that couples well initially but fails later qualification. The opportunity is in selecting the next physical build; customer economics are unverified.
change: Approved adhesive, cure/dispense recipe, attachment geometry and package support.
measure: Per-channel optical loss across assembly and stress, position records and failure analysis.
deliver: An attachment/material recipe retaining the owner's optical margin after required stress.
evidenceSummary: IBM reports package development returning from early stress failures to material/process/structure changes and subsequent passing tests. The proposed LLM integration is not demonstrated.
scope: IBM polymer-waveguide research and vendor assembly capabilities; follow-up evidence outside the accepted Lenovo rack manufacturing graph.

steps.title: Establish optical truth
steps.subtitle: Reference + repeat mates
steps.action: Calibrate the optical path and record channel performance before attachment.
steps.change: Controlled remates and reference specimens.
steps.measure: Insertion loss under defined wavelength/polarization conditions and remating variability.
steps.decision: Can persistent package loss be distinguished from connector or fixture variation?
steps.basis: Proposed baseline around documented optical methods

steps.title: Align and attach
steps.subtitle: Record each transition
steps.action: Build traceable material/process splits using precision stages, vision and controlled bonding.
steps.change: Approved adhesive, dispense geometry, cure and attachment variants.
steps.measure: Loss before, during and after bonding; position and recipe history.
steps.decision: At which physical transition does loss appear?
steps.basis: Assembly capabilities documented; diagnostic policy proposed

steps.title: Apply stress
steps.subtitle: Expose latent drift
steps.action: Run required assembly and reliability exposures with unstressed sister specimens.
steps.change: Exposure status while retaining defined controls and requirements.
steps.measure: Channel-by-channel loss after reflow/stress and approved dimensional or failure analysis.
steps.decision: Is the change persistent, and does it follow a material, structure or recipe factor?
steps.basis: Failure-driven stress testing reported

steps.title: Revise the package
steps.subtitle: New recipe, fresh builds
steps.action: Use stagewise loss and failure evidence to choose an approved material/process/structure change.
steps.change: Build a fresh package variant rather than merely realigning the failed sample.
steps.measure: Actual build genealogy and optical response through the same stages.
steps.decision: Does the revision address the failure without trading it for another weakness?
steps.basis: Physical development return reported; LLM selection proposed

steps.title: Verify retention
steps.subtitle: Independent lots + stress
steps.action: Freeze the recipe and qualify independent builds under unchanged optical limits.
steps.change: Fresh lots and complete required stress.
steps.measure: Post-stress loss, repeatability and reference-path stability.
steps.decision: Accept durable performance, not only time-zero coupling.
steps.basis: Reported retest foundation; owner-specific verification proposed

bench.specimen: A defined optical attachment/package family with traceable channel and process history.
bench.stimulus: Controlled optical input plus the owner's bonding, reflow and environmental-stress sequences.
instruments: Calibrated optical source and power/loss measurement
Stress chambers and approved failure-analysis tools
bench.hard: Precision alignment, active tracking during bonding, dispensing and optical acquisition use specialist equipment.
bench.robot: Transfer carriers and specimens among assembly, stress and optical retest while preserving identity.
bench.flexible: Optional loading or variable connection tasks only. Learned dexterity is not the precision-alignment mechanism.
llmInputs: Failure analysis and prior package changes
bench.llmDecision: Compare bonding, material, structure and fixture explanations; choose the next controlled build and interpret results across stages.
bench.tools: Alignment controllers, optical models, statistical experiment design and fitting provide numerical control and analysis.
bench.wait: Fabrication, adhesive preparation/cure, reflow, reliability exposure and destructive analysis remain. Decisions may occur between lots.

verification: Separate remating variability from persistent package damage.
Test all required assembly and stress stages.
Confirm on independent builds with unchanged optical limits.
baseline: Existing active align/attach/test systems, package engineering, optical modelling and conventional experiment design. These provide a substantial integration baseline.
access: A module/process owner with failed lots, recipe/data access, stress capacity and material/package change rights.
unknowns: Access to an unresolved package campaign
How much latency is reducible engineering work versus exposure
Transfer from the IBM example to the intended package
Incremental LLM benefit and buyer economics
nextTest: Take one post-stress failure family and test whether combined process genealogy and loss history lead to better next-build choices than the current engineering workflow.

name: HBM encapsulant development
title: Improve heat transfer without creating stack defects.
summary: Choose a molded-underfill material and process that survives filling, warpage and package reliability requirements.
problem: A promising material can improve conductivity yet fail when thin dies are stacked and packaged. Material-coupon success is not package success.
value: Resolve a coupled material/process qualification problem in high-value memory packaging. Access, campaign economics and our incremental contribution remain unknown.
change: Owner-approved encapsulant candidates and mold/fill/cure process splits.
measure: Package thermal behavior, warpage, defects and owner-selected electrical/reliability outcomes.
deliver: A repeatable material/process combination that passes package qualification across appropriate lots.
evidenceSummary: SK hynix describes new molding compounds, universal test vehicles, packaging, reliability testing, countermeasures and improved passing materials.
scope: Manufacturer material-development account. Specific instruments below are a proposed implementation, not disclosed SK hynix production equipment.

steps.title: Define material splits
steps.subtitle: Trace formulation + recipe
steps.action: Select approved candidates and representative test vehicles with a production baseline.
steps.change: Material and process factors in a controlled experimental plan.
steps.measure: Material identity, conditioning, geometry and planned build genealogy.
steps.decision: Does the experiment separate material effects from packaging-process changes?
steps.basis: Material and test-vehicle development documented

steps.title: Package test vehicles
steps.subtitle: Use precision equipment
steps.action: Prepare candidate compound and build test vehicles using the owner's packaging line.
steps.change: Approved mold/fill/cure settings and material candidates.
steps.measure: Actual recipe and build conditions; proposed fill/defect and warpage inspection.
steps.decision: Which builds are physically representative and suitable for qualification?
steps.basis: Packaging documented; detailed metrology proposed

steps.title: Measure and stress
steps.subtitle: Thermal + defect outcomes
steps.action: Characterize the package, apply required reliability exposures and repeat relevant measurements.
steps.change: Defined exposure; preserve witness coupons and baseline samples.
steps.measure: Proposed thermal/warpage, acoustic or X-ray inspection and owner-selected electrical tests.
steps.decision: Which failure mechanism limits the otherwise promising material?
steps.basis: Reliability work documented; instrument suite proposed

steps.title: Apply a countermeasure
steps.subtitle: Material or process?
steps.action: Connect failure evidence to a revised formulation or controlled process split.
steps.change: Approved material/process countermeasure and a new traceable build.
steps.measure: Defect recurrence and performance under the original conditions.
steps.decision: Did the countermeasure remove the defect without compromising another requirement?
steps.basis: Physical countermeasure loop reported

steps.title: Qualify the combination
steps.subtitle: Repeat across lots
steps.action: Confirm passing package behavior on independent builds and appropriate lots.
steps.change: Fresh builds with a fixed selected recipe.
steps.measure: Complete owner qualification results, not only conductivity.
steps.decision: Admit a reproducible material/process combination; do not substitute a fast proxy for required reliability tests.
steps.basis: Passing material-development outcome reported; campaign details undisclosed

bench.specimen: Representative stacked-memory test vehicles and controlled material/process splits.
bench.stimulus: The owner's packaging recipe and fixed reliability qualification conditions.
instruments: Proposed thermal characterization and warpage measurement
bench.hard: Specialist wafer/die handling, bonding, molding and process controls are the core physical infrastructure.
bench.robot: Standard carriers and automated transfers between packaging, stress and metrology where supported by the existing line.
bench.flexible: No necessary role established at fragile die interfaces. This candidate is primarily specialist automation plus experiment reasoning.
bench.llmDecision: Reconcile competing material/process explanations, identify confounding factors and propose the next informative experimental split.
bench.tools: Materials models, statistical experiment design and existing process controls provide quantitative analysis and execution.
bench.wait: Material preparation, wafer/package builds, supplier iterations and long reliability tests may dominate.

verification: Use a representative package and production baseline.
Check defects and reliability alongside thermal improvement.
Confirm repeatability across the owner's required lots.
baseline: Manufacturer material engineering, precision packaging equipment, materials informatics and conventional experiment design.
access: Committed manufacturer/material partner, confidential formulation and recipe data, packaging capacity and permission to change them.
unknowns: Proprietary recipes and meaningful action access
nextTest: Partner on a new material/process campaign with real failed test vehicles and compare the quality of next-split decisions against the existing team and tools.

name: High-speed channel correlation
title: Fix the channel—or prove the fixture is wrong.
summary: Separate measurement and model error from a real hardware problem before committing to a new board or interconnect.
owner: Signal-integrity team with channel and fixture ownership
problem: Measured loss or receiver behavior disagrees with the model. Fixture contacts, calibration, de-embedding and actual geometry can all be plausible causes.
value: Avoid a false hardware redesign while verifying real link performance. The cost and recurrence of that problem have not been measured in an owner campaign.
change: Controlled remates, reference fixtures, channel/launch variants and measured model inputs.
measure: Calibrated S-parameters, mating repeatability, geometry and actual receiver error performance.
deliver: A verified channel correction—or evidence that the original channel needs no redesign.
evidenceSummary: Samtec describes modeled/measured fixture development, configurable channel lengths and precision compression interfaces. The broader diagnostic bench is proposed.
scope: Follow-up fixture research, not a confirmed NVLink manufacturing or automated diagnostic route. Higher-speed pathfinding is not a demonstrated production result.

steps.title: Establish reference planes
steps.subtitle: Calibration + repeatability
steps.action: Calibrate the measurement chain and repeatedly measure reference standards and controlled mates.
steps.change: Repeat connections with defined compression and geometry.
steps.measure: S-parameter uncertainty and connection repeatability.
steps.decision: Can the discrepancy be explained by the measurement chain?
steps.basis: Fixture-method foundation; diagnostic baseline proposed

steps.title: Compare model and build
steps.subtitle: Use actual geometry
steps.action: Compare measured response with a model tied to the real specimen and calibration history.
steps.change: Known channel lengths and characterized fixture or launch variants.
steps.measure: Model residuals, fixture behavior and available dimensional metrology.
steps.decision: Does the discrepancy track the fixture, the channel or a modeling assumption?
steps.basis: Modeled/measured development documented; causal policy proposed

steps.title: Run a discriminating swap
steps.subtitle: Reference or new channel
steps.action: Choose a characterized reference or channel specimen that separates competing explanations.
steps.change: One fixture/sample family at a time; order a revised board only when justified.
steps.measure: Recalibrated response after the swap and its repeatability.
steps.decision: Is a hardware change supported, or should the fixture/model be corrected?
steps.basis: Proposed experimental selection

steps.title: Test the actual link
steps.subtitle: Receiver + traffic
steps.action: Validate with representative receiver hardware and approved traffic/crosstalk conditions.
steps.change: Held-out lanes and operating conditions within the owner envelope.
steps.measure: Bit-error and eye behavior; distinguish measured errors from model-based metrics.
steps.decision: Does the proposed correction improve actual product behavior?
steps.basis: Proposed product verification; not established by the fixture paper

steps.title: Confirm independently
steps.subtitle: Fresh boards + calibration
steps.action: Repeat on independent specimens and, where feasible, an independent fixture/calibration path.
steps.change: Fresh boards and repeated mates with fixed acceptance limits.
steps.measure: Repeatability and representative link performance.
steps.decision: Release only within measured bandwidth and verified product conditions.
steps.basis: Proposed verification campaign

bench.specimen: An editable channel with characterized launches, fixtures and representative receiver hardware.
bench.stimulus: Calibrated network-analyzer sweeps and defined link traffic/crosstalk.
instruments: Vector network analyzer and reference standards
TDR where suitable and dimensional metrology
Repeatable compression and protected RF connections
bench.hard: Calibration, defined mating force/torque, instrument sequencing and numerical de-embedding.
bench.robot: Potential standardized specimen exchange and compression mating, after repeatability is proven.
bench.flexible: No demonstrated necessity. Expert setup and protected precision interfaces take priority over dexterity.
bench.llmDecision: Choose the next reference or specimen test that distinguishes a measurement artifact from a real design problem.
bench.tools: EM simulation, calibration/de-embedding and numerical correlation perform the quantitative analysis.
bench.wait: Board fabrication, fixture calibration and long error-rate acquisitions remain.

verification: Confirm model-based conclusions on actual receiver hardware.
Use independent specimens and a second calibration path where feasible.
baseline: Expert RF calibration, EM simulation, configurable fixtures and existing signal-integrity analysis tools.
access: Raw calibration/model files, representative devices, measured geometry and authority to build channel variants.
unknowns: Which intervention actually separates the causes
Avoided redesign cost and LLM contribution
nextTest: Take a known fixture-origin and a known channel-origin failure, hide their causes, and compare diagnosis and unnecessary redesigns under identical instrumentation.

name: Fan geometry and acoustics
title: Reduce loaded noise without losing airflow.
summary: Connect simulation, physical prototypes and measurements to correct a fan's behavior at the actual operating point.
owner: Fan development team with CAD and prototype access
problem: A design looks acceptable in free air or simulation but misses the required noise, flow or strength envelope under representative resistance and mounting.
value: Reduce unproductive prototype changes while preserving performance. The development loop is well documented; a distinctive advantage for our system is not.
change: Impeller/frame geometry, approved materials, mounting and speed/control variants.
measure: Pressure-flow curves, loaded acoustic spectra, vibration, speed, power and temperature.
deliver: A production-representative design meeting the required airflow, noise and strength envelope.
evidenceSummary: SANYO DENKI documents simulation, physical prototypes, acoustic/flow measurements and feedback into development. Existing optimization is a strong baseline.
scope: Manufacturer development methods and example products; the supplier of the selected Lenovo fan is not established.

steps.title: Set the operating point
steps.subtitle: Load + mounting
steps.action: Define the customer resistance, acoustic limits and representative mounting.
steps.change: Controlled speed and resistance sweeps.
steps.measure: Baseline pressure-flow and loaded noise behavior.
steps.decision: Where does the candidate miss the required envelope?
steps.basis: Documented development measurements

steps.title: Predict a revision
steps.subtitle: Model + physical evidence
steps.action: Compare simulation with acoustic, vibration and airflow observations.
steps.change: Candidate geometry/material or mounting hypotheses.
steps.measure: Model/measurement mismatch and the relevant spectral or flow features.
steps.decision: Which change is supported, and which experiment would distinguish a rotor, mounting or model issue?
steps.basis: Simulation feedback documented; LLM cause selection proposed

steps.title: Build the prototype
steps.subtitle: Print + assemble + inspect
steps.action: Produce and assemble a traceable impeller/frame variant through a qualified prototype path.
steps.change: Geometry or approved material/process variant.
steps.measure: Actual geometry, assembly quality and required pre-test checks.
steps.decision: Is this a representative, testable physical revision?
steps.basis: Physical prototyping documented

steps.title: Measure under load
steps.subtitle: Acoustics + flow + vibration
steps.action: Repeat the same operating envelope and compare with the baseline.
steps.change: The prototype; retain comparable mounting and test conditions.
steps.measure: Pressure-flow curve, loaded spectra, vibration, speed/current and temperature.
steps.decision: Was noise reduced without sacrificing required airflow or other limits?
steps.basis: Documented measurement and development return

steps.title: Verify production parts
steps.subtitle: Molded samples + repeat runs
steps.action: Confirm the design on production-representative parts and the intended installation.
steps.change: Fresh samples and the actual material/process route.
steps.measure: Required pressure/flow, acoustic and strength results.
steps.decision: A successful printed prototype alone is insufficient for release.
steps.basis: Proposed verification campaign grounded in development methods

bench.specimen: A fan family with editable impeller/frame CAD and a representative customer mounting.
bench.stimulus: Controlled speed, flow resistance and selected temperature/strength conditions.
bench.hard: Repeatable mounting, electrical connection, speed/load sweeps and automated measurements.
bench.robot: Load interchangeable carriers and transfer qualified samples between stations if throughput warrants it.
bench.flexible: Possible variable harness presentation; unnecessary with a standardized carrier.
bench.llmDecision: Interpret conflicts between predictions and physical results and propose a test that separates geometry, mounting and sample defects.
bench.tools: Existing fluid/motor simulation and numerical geometry optimization remain the quantitative engines.
bench.wait: Prototype printing/finishing, assembly, stabilization, strength tests and molded sample availability remain.

verification: Compare within the same loaded operating envelope.
Preserve airflow and strength while reducing noise.
baseline: Existing automatic simulation/optimization, load-noise mapping and acoustic/vibration inspection; incremental orchestration value must be demonstrated.
access: Editable CAD, raw flow/acoustic data, a safe prototype route and production-representative samples.
nextTest: Use a real loaded-noise failure to compare next-prototype choices and final verified performance against the current design team and optimizer.
